social.text: The Dialogue Panel gives you what actors have always had: sides. A voice scattered across a whole script is hard to hear as one person. Strip the script to nothing but talking. Turn one character on alone, or two, and read the relationship: who asks, who interrupts, who never finishes a sentence. "They all sound the same" is the note that kills scripts. Here, you catch it in seconds. # screenwriting constructurescreenwriter.com # screenwriter # screenplay # filmmaking # filmmaker

social.text: The Dead Darlings Panel is a morgue where the dead can come back. Every writer keeps a graveyard: a file called cuts, the back page of a notebook. Lines too good to delete and too wrong to keep. When a line's like that, send it to Dead Darlings instead of deleting it. Out of the script, not gone. Bring it back whenever the moment argues for it.
